item.title: Proton Competition Induced Stabilization in TEMPO‐Based Redox‐Targeting Flow Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a proton-competition strategy using polyaniline as a solid redox-targeting material to stabilize TEMPO radicals without molecular engineering. This suppresses hydrogenation via PANI's reversible doping/de-doping, enabling 4.37-fold capacity enhancement, 99.99% coulombic efficiency, and 99.94% capacity retention per cycle over 500 cycles. It provides design principles for stable, long-duration aqueous organic redox flow batteries.

item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in an ultrafast, spontaneous implosion-popcorn reaction that disintegrates centimeter-scale precursors into ultrafine particles within seconds, creating a homogeneous tri-phase Fe/Li₃P/Li alloy with an interpenetrating network. This shifts alloy fabrication from passive to active, efficient, and uniform. Significance: enhanced Young's modulus, versatile processability (slurries, foils, powders), and stable cycling over 3000 h via regulated Li nucleation and uniform growth.

item.title: Sabatier Principle‐Guided Co‐Solvent Selection for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zinc Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work introduces a Sabatier-principle-analogous framework using molecular polarity index (MPI) as a quantitative descriptor for rational co-solvent selection in aqueous zinc batteries, revealing a volcano-type MPI–performance relationship. The optimal intermediate polarity balances interfacial homogeneity and kinetics, enabling ultralong cycling and high-loading pouch cells, and successfully predicts 1,2,4-butanetriol as a new efficient co-solvent, transforming electrolyte formulation from empirical to predictive.
🏷 aqueous zinc battery · co-solvent electrolyte · molecular polarity index · Sabatier principle · Zn anode stability
